**sdd/issue-887-lane-collector/apply-progress**

**What**: Slice A of #887 (the lane collector's pure planner), plus a full cold-review correction batch (issue #897, batch 2). Batch 1: `brain/scripts/memory/lane/plan.mjs` (`planLaneCommit`) + `plan.test.mjs` (19 cases) + A7's `canonicalOrNull` move to `format.mjs`. Commits `04b50227`/`96f18830`/`094d1b11`. tasks.md A1.1-A1.4, A2.1, A3.1 all `[x]`. Batch 2 (this update) applied 12 cold-review corrections (C1-C7, E1-E3, E5-E6) on top, in 4 more commits on the same worktree/branch: `da3b874a` (docs: copied explore/proposal/spec/design/tasks.md read-only from the sibling Slice-B worktree so the SDD contract rides PR A too), `5b8e5c27` (test: C1-C4 pins — validateRecord gate, skipped.sort, files.sort, slug-truncation-lands-on-dash — each verified by manually mutating plan.mjs, confirming the new test kills the mutant, then reverting before commit), `05e9a7dc` (fix: C5/C6/E1/E2/E6 — see Why below), `a0f546bc` (refactor: C7 one canonicalOrNull definition via format.mjs import in split-records.mjs; E3 purity-guard hardening; E5 dropped planLaneCommit's dead `commit: null` return field after confirming Slice B's collect.mjs never reads it).

**Why**: Fresh cold review of already-`[x]`-ticked Slice A work found real gaps STRICT TDD hadn't caught: C1/C2/C3/C4 were true behavior the 19-case suite never exercised (each pin's mutant survived the old suite); C5/C6 were genuine bugs — `duplicates` occurrences were registered unconditionally BEFORE the C5 secret-winner guard ran, so a group whose winner was secret-skipped was still counted as a duplicate (over-report), while a secret-marked LOSER in an otherwise-clean group was silently dropped with no `skipped` entry anywhere (under-report — C6). Root cause for both: the code consulted only the winner's secret status for routing but registered occurrence bookkeeping for the WHOLE group before that check ran. Fix: push a `secret` skip for every marked member (winner or loser) first, then only register `duplicates` occurrences after the winner clears the secret guard.

**Where**: brain/scripts/memory/lane/plan.mjs, brain/scripts/memory/lane/plan.test.mjs, brain/scripts/memory/lib/split-records.mjs, openspec/changes/issue-887-lane-collector/{explore,proposal,spec,design,tasks,apply-progress}.md (apply-progress.md untracked by design, same as batch 1).

**Learned**: (1) A stability-fixture-embedded sort assertion is not automatically mutant-killing — C3's first attempt (assert sortedness inside the big A1.3 permutation test) did NOT kill the `files.sort()`-removed mutant, because that fixture's candidate paths all share one uniform `.memory/records/` prefix, so file-key sort order already coincided with path sort order; a SEPARATE deterministic test with basename-order and path-order deliberately disagreeing was needed to actually exercise the sort. (2) Before dropping the planner's `commit: null` field (E5), checked the sibling worktree's in-progress `collect.mjs` (Slice B, uncommitted) directly — confirmed it builds its own return object with its own `commit` key after running `commit-tree`, never reads `plan.commit`, so the drop is safe; flagged as a risk anyway in case Slice B's shell changes before merge. (3) design.md's output shape never listed `commit` in the first place — batch 1's placeholder was itself the deviation, not this drop. (4) X1 (post the #889 lane-paths sentence) remains open across both batches — no GitHub-write scope in either. Focused suite 101/101, full `npm test` 4953/4953 green after every commit.
